question: Compare how Schwab and Raymond James describe their value proposition to independent advisors.

claims.text: Schwab: The 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 26, 2026) states Schwab built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed, and that today it serves more than 16,000 firms with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.

Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, Item 1) states Schwab's sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients, and that it provides a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering clients' assets easily and efficiently.

Schwab: The May 2026 investor day deck (p.23) describes Schwab as the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.

Schwab: A Schwab spokesperson said (trade press, August 26, 2026) that few firms can bring together custody, trading, banking, lending, wealth management, workplace and retail investing at Schwab's scale and value with the best client service, and that Schwab invests in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow.

Schwab: CEO Rick Wurster said (trade press, October 28, 2026) that Schwab's role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps advisors support their clients and helps their firms thrive.

Schwab: The 3Q26 deck (period ended September 26, 2026, p.13) describes its differentiated, full-service platform to advisors as built on scale and reputation, breadth beyond custody, operational excellence, and dedicated service and support.

Schwab: The 3Q25 transcript (period ended September 25, 2025) states Schwab deepens relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.

Schwab: The 1Q26 transcript (period ended March 26, 2026) states Schwab's CEO said its value proposition to advisers has never been stronger, citing added lending capabilities such as a structured asset lending program.

Schwab: The 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 26, 2026) states Schwab's CEO said its capabilities are hard to match in terms of service, breadth of capabilities, banking and lending, AI innovations, and advice and consulting support, which is why it is number one in the space.

Schwab: The 4Q25 transcript (period ended December 25, 2025) states Schwab's CEO said it is hard for other firms to compete with Schwab's size, scale, and the breadth and strength of its capabilities in custody, consulting and advice, and product.

Raymond James: The independent advisor recruiting page (page content as of May 19, 2026) frames its value proposition as a partnership in independence, offering independent contractors access to the firm's full capabilities at a level right for their business.

Raymond James: The independent advisor page (page content as of May 19, 2026) describes powerful independence — the ability to serve clients and grow an independent practice without wanting for capability, expert insight or client resources, with everything the firm has available on demand.

Raymond James: The independent advisor page (page content as of May 19, 2026) describes enjoying the rewards of running one's own practice with the support of a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer, spanning investing, planning, private wealth, marketing and technology.

Raymond James: CEO Paul Shoukry described (4Q25 transcript, period ended December 25, 2025) the value proposition as a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, which combined with a strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Raymond James: Shoukry described (2Q25 transcript, period ended June 25, 2025) the firm's best-of-both-worlds value proposition — a unique combination of advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions — as resonating with advisors across all affiliation options, with the strong balance sheet and commitment to independence increasingly a differentiator.

Raymond James: Shoukry stated (1Q26 transcript, period ended March 26, 2026) that advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities — Raymond James offers a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture together with leading technologies, products and solutions, plus a strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence.

Raymond James: The affiliation options page (page content as of April 21, 2026) describes the power of choice — AdvisorChoice lets advisors match their goals to an affiliation option offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility, backed by a leading independent financial firm.

Raymond James: Shoukry described (4Q25 transcript, period ended December 25, 2025) the powerfully personal value proposition released with the firm's annual report — focusing on personal relationships with financial advisors and giving them tools to strengthen relationships with clients — as increasingly differentiating and resonating with existing and prospective advisors.

Raymond James: Shoukry described (3Q25 transcript, period ended September 25, 2025) a stable, long-term platform as what resonates most with advisors — Raymond James's best-of-both-worlds value proposition (advisor/client-focused culture and long-term client-first values coupled with resources, platform, technology, products and services) versus short-term, levered players in an industry with M&A consolidation.

Raymond James: The investor day deck (June 2025, p.91) quotes advisors describing the firm's culture of promoting independence and putting advisors and clients first, along with world-class technology that creates capacity and frees time to spend with clients.

Schwab and Raymond James: The two firms' value propositions to independent advisors can be compared side by side on the shared themes of custody/platform breadth, service, and technology, but they are framed differently and so are not directly rankable on a single shared scale. Schwab (described in its own terms, various periods through September 26, 2026) frames its offer as a custody-plus platform: a full-service platform and RIA support ecosystem built on scale and reputation, breadth beyond custody (custody, trading, banking, lending, wealth tools, investment/lending products, technology), operational excellence, and dedicated service and support, with the stated goal of helping independent advisors grow, compete, and succeed without dictating how large they should be. Raymond James (described in its own terms, various periods through June 26, 2026) frames its independent contractor offer as a partnership in independence and a best-of-both-worlds value proposition centered on an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology, products and solutions, plus a strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, and emphasizes offering all affiliation options (employee, independent contractor, RIA custody) at scale. The definitions differ in emphasis — Schwab leads with the breadth and scale of its platform and ecosystem beyond custody, while Raymond James leads with culture and freedom within independence — and the two are not stated in a common metric, so the comparison holds qualitatively on these shared themes but not as a one-for-one ranking.
